thread.title: Walmart Streaming Service? Retailer Mulls Challenge To Netflix, Amazon: Report

author: ELAINE LOW
title: Walmart Streaming Service? Retailer Mulls Challenge To Netflix, Amazon: Report
text:
Could a Walmart ( WMT ) streaming service become a reality, giving Netflix ( NFLX ) and Amazon ( AMZN ) Prime Video a run for their money?
X The nation's biggest retailer is mulling the creation of its own subscription streaming video service, according to The Information , citing people familiar with the matter.
Amazon.com's video library comes with its annual $119 Prime membership, which costs $12.99 on a monthly basis. (It also offers a stand-alone subscription to just its Prime Video offerings.) Netflix costs anywhere from $7.99 a month for a basic plan to $13.99 a month for a premium subscription.
But a Walmart streaming service, if it comes to fruition, would reportedly be priced at only $8 a month.
Shares closed up 0.6% on the stock market today , Netflix fell 5.2% after reporting disappointing subscriber growth, and Amazon rose 1.2% following strong Prime Day sales.

Please contact customer service CLOSE The Other Walmart Streaming Service Walmart already operates Vudu, which the retailer calls an "online video store" that allows viewers to rent and purchase individual titles. It also sells the Vudu Spark streaming stick.
A new streaming service would deepen Walmart's presence in an ultracompetitive space, with rivals to Netflix and Amazon making their own big moves.
Disney ( DIS ) launched its ESPN+ streaming service earlier this year, and it is preparing for the 2019 debut of its own stand-alone, Disney-branded streaming service that will feature content from Marvel, Pixar and Lucasfilm.
Hulu, which is jointly owned by Disney and other media outlets, has been expanding in original content, and Apple ( AAPL ) is ramping up its video offerings as well.
But the Bentonville, Ark.-based mega-retailer appears to be challenging Amazon from a number of different angles, aside from a potential Walmart streaming service.
Earlier Tuesday, Walmart and Microsoft ( MSFT ) announced a five-year partnership , in which the massive big-box retailer will use the tech giant's cloud services and productivity tools. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said both companies' rivalries with Amazon were "absolutely core" to the deal.
